findings: src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp TrySetExactBloomFilter: the switch uses key_type.InternalType(), so DECIMAL, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP*, ENUM and similar logical types with INT16/INT32/INT64/UINT8.. storage all qualify for exact mode. Their min/max are then read with Value::GetValue<int64_t>/<uint64_t>, which goes through Value::GetValueInternal and does a logical cast, not a read of the raw storage. For DECIMAL it casts to DOUBLE and then rounds to an integer: build keys 1.00 and 2.00 in DECIMAL(15,2) (stored as 100 and 200) give min_key=1 and max_key=2, so only 2 bits are allocated. TemplatedInsertKeysFromRows then reads raw 100, computes offset 99 >= 2 and throws InternalException('Exact bloom filter key outside of the build-side min/max range'). Any equi-join on a DECIMAL key with a dense, selective build side fails the query. For DATE/TIMESTAMP, Cast::Operation<date_t,int64_t> (and the like) is not a raw reinterpretation. It either throws or gives a value that does not match the stored int32/int64, so a join on a date key such as o_orderdate = d_date with a pushed BF errors or computes a wrong range. The author's tests only covered plain integer logical types.

If no exception is thrown, there is still a mismatch: the probe side (TemplatedExactLookup / FilterValue) uses raw physical values, while the range comes from logical-cast values. Any type where the two differ breaks the 'no false negatives' requirement of the filter.

Otherwise the mechanism looks sound. The bitmap is shared by reference. A single-condition join with NULLs not equal is required, the has_cast check makes the probe type match, NULLs are rejected on both sides, inserts are atomic under parallel finalize, and memory is capped at 512MiB / 16B per row. Nothing in it is specific to the benchmark.
required_changes: Allow exact mode only for plain integer logical types (TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT, UTINYINT, USMALLINT, UINTEGER, UBIGINT), switching on key_type.id(). Alternatively, read min/max as raw physical values (e.g. Value::GetValueUnsafe<T>() for the matching physical T), so the range is in the same domain as the stored keys and the probe vectors. DECIMAL/DATE/TIMESTAMP/ENUM keys must either work correctly or fall back to the hashed BF.
Add a test with an equi-join on DECIMAL and on DATE keys whose build side is dense and selective enough to trigger a BF. The results must match the run with join_filter_pushdown disabled.
